## Overview

CERTH's Open Science commitments, aligned with the
[European Open Science Cloud (EOSC)](https://eosc.eu/) and Horizon Europe requirements, encourage
making software developed in the course of publicly funded research available as open source wherever
possible.

Licence selection should involve a consultation with the CERTH OSPO. When selecting a licence,
consider:

- **Community norms** within your ecosystem
- **Which sharing regime** (permissive, weakly-reciprocal, or strongly-reciprocal) aligns with your
  project's objectives
- **Obligations imposed by your funding body** or consortium agreement

The CERTH OSPO team is available at **ospo@certh.gr** for guidance.

## Licensing Software

Use a licence approved by the [Open Source Initiative (OSI)](https://opensource.org/licenses) for
CERTH-copyrighted software. Common choices:

| Licence | Type | Typical use case |
|---|---|---|
| Apache-2.0 | Permissive | General software; maximum adoption; includes patent grant |
| MIT | Permissive | Small utilities and libraries; minimal requirements |
| GPL-3.0 | Strongly reciprocal | Tools where all derivatives must remain open source |
| LGPL-3.0 | Weakly reciprocal | Libraries intended to be linked from proprietary software |
| EUPL-1.2 | Weakly reciprocal | EU public-sector software; compatible with GPL and AGPL |

The **EUPL-1.2** is worth particular attention for CERTH projects. It was designed for European public
bodies, is legally valid across all EU member states, and is explicitly compatible with the GPL-2.0,
GPL-3.0, and AGPL-3.0, as well as the EUPL itself.

## Licensing Documentation

Per the European Open Access mandate and EOSC principles, the recommended licence for documentation
and written outputs is [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC-BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
This allows broad reuse with attribution and is accepted by most research funders, including the
European Research Council (ERC) and Horizon Europe.

## Licensing Datasets

For datasets, consider:

- **CC0 1.0** — public domain dedication; no restrictions on reuse; preferred when maximum data
  sharing is the goal
- **CC-BY 4.0** — attribution required; appropriate when institutional credit is important

Be aware that some datasets may contain personal data subject to GDPR. Consult CERTH's Data
Protection Officer before releasing datasets that could contain or be derived from personal
information.

## Multiple Licences in One Project

Projects that combine software, documentation, and data assets will typically carry multiple licences
— one per component type. The REUSE specification makes this manageable by allowing per-file licence
declarations rather than a single project-wide licence. See the
[Copyright recommendations](copyright.qmd) page for implementation details.

## Licence Compatibility

When combining components under different licences, compatibility must be verified before release.
A common compatibility matrix:

| You want to use... | Under Apache-2.0 | Under MIT | Under GPL-3.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apache-2.0 code | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| MIT code | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| GPL-3.0 code | Only if your project is also GPL-3.0 | Only if your project is also GPL-3.0 | ✓ |
| LGPL-3.0 library | ✓ (dynamic linking) | ✓ (dynamic linking) | ✓ |

When in doubt, the CERTH OSPO can review your dependency graph and advise on compatibility.
